channel.title: Sarasota Flooring Company — flooring answers
channel.description: Flooring questions from Sarasota and Gulf Coast homeowners, answered.

item.title: What's the Best Flooring Option for a House by the Water?
item.description: For a home directly on the water in Sarasota or Manatee County, porcelain tile is the flooring pros reach for most often: it resists the 0.5% water-absorption test that defines porcelain, and it shrugs off sand, wet guests and open-window humidity that wear down wood. Below the base flood elevation, FEMA's guidance only allows its top two damage-resistance classes, so ask your flood consultant before installing anything else there.

item.title: Which Is Better in Florida Humidity, Waterproof Laminate or LVP?
item.description: Waterproof laminate and luxury vinyl plank cost about the same — This Old House puts laminate installed at $5-$12/sq ft and vinyl plank at $5-$20/sq ft. Their warranties differ more: Pergo's WetProtect laminate covers spills and pet accidents but excludes flooding and standing water. Our verdict: LVP is the safer pick near Sarasota-area kitchens, bathrooms and lanais; laminate works fine in drier living spaces.

item.title: Can Water-Damaged Hardwood Floors Be Saved?
item.description: Often, yes, if the moisture source gets fixed first and nobody sands the boards too early. Mild cupping can flatten on its own over several weeks to months once moisture-meter readings return to normal; sanding before that point tends to cause crowning instead. Angi's 2026 data puts average hardwood floor repair cost at $1,078 nationally, with a typical range of $482 to $1,707.

item.title: Can Vinyl Plank Flooring Be Saved After a Flood?
item.description: Sometimes, if the water was clean and you act fast. Click-together vinyl plank can often be lifted, cleaned, dried and relaid, but the pad or cork underlayment beneath it should be discarded and the slab dried and retested before reinstalling. Water contaminated by storm surge or sewage, common after a Sarasota-area hurricane, usually means the flooring needs to be replaced rather than salvaged.

item.title: Is Vinyl Plank Flooring Actually Waterproof?
item.description: Yes at the surface, but not automatically underneath: in a Sarasota-area home on a slab, most floating LVP/LVT makers still cap allowable moisture at 75-85% relative humidity, so a waterproof plank doesn't remove the need for a dry slab. After a clean-water event, planks can often be lifted, dried and re-laid within the EPA's 24-48 hour mold-prevention window.

item.title: Why Does Vinyl Plank Flooring Buckle or Peak?
item.description: In Sarasota-area homes, vinyl plank floors usually buckle because they have nowhere to expand: COREtec's install guide calls for a 1/4-inch gap at every wall, and planks pinned tight by trim, door jambs or a glued transition strip peak first, especially in sun-heated rooms. An uneven slab makes it worse — Shaw's SPC guide requires the concrete to be flat within 3/16 inch over 10 feet before installation.

item.title: Can You Use a Steam Mop on Vinyl Plank or Hardwood Floors?
item.description: No, not on vinyl plank or hardwood. Shaw's resilient flooring care guide says plainly not to use steam cleaners on resilient flooring, and Angi warns steam can warp planks and break down the seam adhesive. Hardwood faces the same risk from heat and trapped moisture. Steam damage isn't covered under a manufacturer's warranty or our 2-year workmanship warranty, so a damp microfiber mop is the safer routine for Sarasota-area homes.

item.title: How Many Sandings Does Your Floor Have Left In It?
item.description: In a Sarasota-area home, solid 3/4 in. hardwood can typically be refinished about 4 times over its life, sometimes up to 10 light screen-and-recoats. Engineered hardwood is more limited: a 2mm wear layer supports 1-2 sandings, 3mm supports 2-3, and 4mm supports 3-4, since each full sanding removes roughly 0.5mm to 1mm of wood.

item.title: What Wear Layer Thickness Do You Actually Need?
item.description: Engineered hardwood wear layers typically run 2mm to 4mm thick. A 2mm layer supports one or two sandings, 3mm supports two or three, and 4mm supports three or four - each full sanding removes roughly 0.5mm to 1mm of wood. If you want your floor refinished more than once, ask for at least a 3mm wear layer before you buy.

item.title: How Do You Test a Concrete Slab for Moisture Before Installing Flooring?
item.description: Concrete slabs get tested with ASTM F2170 relative humidity probes, set at 40% of slab depth, or ASTM F1869 calcium chloride tests measuring vapor emission over 24 hours. The default acceptable reading is 75% RH or 3 lbs per 1,000 sq ft per 24 hours, unless the flooring manufacturer specifies a higher limit, and we run this before quoting any wood or vinyl job on a Sarasota-area slab.

item.title: Does Direct Sunlight Damage Vinyl Plank Floors?
item.description: Yes. Both COREtec and Shaw's care guides warn against prolonged direct sunlight on vinyl plank, since heat buildup can discolor the wear layer and cause thermal expansion at sliding doors. Sarasota-area rooms with unshaded west-facing glass are most at risk. UV-blocking window film runs roughly $200-$500 per window, a common fix homeowners pair with drapes or blinds during peak sun hours.

item.title: Which Vinyl Plank Core Handles Florida Heat Better, SPC or WPC?
item.description: SPC (stone-plastic composite) tolerates Florida heat better than WPC (wood-plastic composite): COREtec rates its SPC lines for -25°F to 155°F after installation, versus just 32°F to 100°F for WPC lines, and only floating installs are approved for three-season rooms with no climate control. Our verdict: pick SPC for a lanai, Florida room, or garage-adjacent space; WPC suits air-conditioned living areas.

item.title: How Soon Do I Have to Pull Up Wet Flooring After Storm Surge?
item.description: Within 24 to 48 hours, per EPA guidance on water-damaged materials, is the window before mold risk climbs sharply. After storm surge specifically, that clock starts as soon as it's safe to re-enter the home, not once power or contractors are available. Helene's 2024 surge alone damaged an estimated 7,600 residences in unincorporated Sarasota County, which is why fast removal matters across an entire neighborhood, not just one house.

item.title: Solid or Engineered Hardwood: Which One Handles a Slab?
item.description: Engineered hardwood is the better choice on a concrete slab in Sarasota and Manatee counties. NWFA guidance says solid wood shouldn't go below grade, and most local homes are slab-on-grade. Engineered hardwood over a slab that tests at or below 75% relative humidity (ASTM F2170) runs about $9-$20 per sq ft installed in 2026.

item.title: What Should I Set My AC and Humidistat to When I Leave My Florida Home for the Summer?
item.description: Leave the AC running at 85°F or lower, per UF/IFAS guidance for closing a seasonal home, since higher settings let indoor humidity pass 55-60% and put wood floors at risk. Southwest Florida HVAC companies recommend a tighter 78-80°F thermostat with the humidistat near 55-60%, calibrated before you leave for the summer.

item.title: Is It Worth Replacing Your Floors Before You List Your House?
item.description: It depends on your floor's condition, not a blanket rule. If flooring is worn, stained or visibly dated, replacing it before listing usually pays for itself; the 2022 NAR/NARI Remodeling Impact Report found new wood flooring recovered 118% of its cost at resale. If your existing floor is in decent shape, a refinish or targeted repair is often the better return for less money and less time before closing.

item.title: Can I Replace My Florida Condo's Carpet With Tile or Hardwood?
item.description: Yes, in most Florida condos you can swap carpet for tile or hardwood, but Florida Statute 718.113 lets your association's declaration control the swap, not the statute itself. Expect to submit an application, meet your building's IIC/STC minimum, 50 at a minimum under Florida's building code, and install an approved acoustic underlayment before the floor goes down.

item.title: Can You Have Real Hardwood Floors in Florida?
item.description: Yes -- solid hardwood can work in a Sarasota or Manatee County home, but only above grade with air conditioning holding steady. NWFA guidelines put hardwood's comfort zone at 30-50% relative humidity and 60-80°F, and any concrete slab must test at or below 75% RH (ASTM F2170) before engineered hardwood glues down directly.

item.title: What Should You Ask a Flooring Contractor Before You Hire One?
item.description: Before hiring a flooring contractor in Sarasota or Manatee County, ask for a written itemized quote covering material, labor, removal and prep, proof of general liability insurance and workers' compensation, and how they test slab moisture. ASTM F2170 caps in-slab relative humidity at 75% before flooring goes down unless the manufacturer allows a higher reading.

item.title: Does Vinyl Plank Work on a Staircase?
item.description: Vinyl plank can go on stairs, but it must be fully glued down, not floated, and most LVP lines don't include a matching stair-nose profile that meets Florida's 3/4 in. to 1-1/4 in. nosing code. Many Sarasota-area homeowners end up with hardwood or engineered treads stained to match instead, since glued-on vinyl nosings tend to work loose within a year or two.

item.title: Can You Put Vinyl Plank Flooring on a Lanai or Florida Room With No AC?
item.description: In a Sarasota-area lanai or Florida room with no AC, yes — if you choose the right core and float it rather than glue it: COREtec approves those spaces only for floating installs, rating SPC for -25°F to 155°F versus just 32°F to 100°F for WPC. Direct sun still matters separately, so an unshaded lanai needs film or blinds even with the right core.

item.title: What Does Porcelain Tile Installation Cost Per Square Foot?
item.description: Installed porcelain or ceramic tile typically runs $6 to $15 per square foot in Sarasota and Manatee County in 2026. Standard 12-18 in. tile costs $6-$10, large-format 24 in.-plus tile costs $9-$15, and wood-look plank tile costs $8-$13. Large-format tile costs more because it demands a flatter substrate and more precise layout to avoid lippage.

item.title: Is a Permit Required to Replace Flooring in Sarasota County?
item.description: Sarasota County generally treats flooring replacement, tile, vinyl plank, hardwood or laminate, as cosmetic work that doesn't require a building permit, as long as there's no change to the subfloor structure or layout. Condo buildings are the exception: HOA rules on sound underlayment can still apply even when the county doesn't require a permit. Confirm specifics with the county building department for your address.

item.title: Does Changing Your Condo's Flooring Need a Permit in Florida?
item.description: It depends on your city and your association. Several Florida cities, including Miami, Miami Beach, Boca Raton and Tampa, require a building permit plus an acoustic affidavit for hard-surface flooring in condos. Regardless of local permit rules, the Florida Building Code requires floor-ceiling assemblies between dwelling units to meet IIC and STC ratings of 50, or 45 if field-tested, which is what most HOA flooring rules are built around.

item.title: Does Replacing Your Flooring Actually Add Home Value?
item.description: Yes, and refinishing pays back more than replacing. The 2022 National Association of Realtors/NARI Remodeling Impact Report found hardwood floor refinishing recovered 147% of its cost at resale, while installing new wood flooring recovered 118%. A typical $3,400 refinish added about $5,000 in perceived value, according to the same report.

item.title: Can Mold Grow Under Vinyl Plank Flooring on a Florida Slab?
item.description: Yes -- mold can grow under vinyl plank on a Florida slab when the concrete emits moisture above the flooring's rated limit, commonly 75% to 85% relative humidity. Floating installation doesn't remove this risk, it just changes how the failure shows up. The EPA says materials should dry within 24-48 hours after any water event to keep mold from establishing.

item.title: Do I Need a Moisture Barrier Under Vinyl Plank on a Concrete Slab?
item.description: It depends on the product, but often yes. Most floating LVP and LVT makers cap acceptable in-slab relative humidity at 75% to 85%; some rigid SPC lines allow up to 90% RH or 8 lbs per 1,000 sq ft per 24 hours within the manufacturer's tested system. A slab above the rated limit needs a vapor-retarder layer before vinyl plank goes down in a Sarasota-area home.

item.title: Do You Need a Moisture Barrier Under Laminate on a Concrete Floor?
item.description: Yes, in a Sarasota-area home on a slab. Mohawk's laminate installation guide requires a moisture barrier over any concrete floor — 6-mil polyethylene film with seams overlapped 8 inches for a floating install. The slab should also test within ASTM F1869's default limit of 3 lbs of moisture vapor emission per 1,000 sq ft per 24 hours, unless the manufacturer allows a higher reading.

item.title: LVP or Porcelain Tile: Which Is Better for a Florida House?
item.description: For most Sarasota-area homes, LVP installs faster and costs less than porcelain tile — a two-person crew can lay about 1,000 square feet of click LVP in 1-2 days on a flat, prepped slab, while tile takes longer because of cure times. Our verdict: choose LVP for speed and warmth underfoot, porcelain for wet areas and long-term durability.

item.title: Is LVP or Tile the Smarter Pick for a Long-Term Rental?
item.description: For a long-term Florida rental, 20-mil rigid-core LVP typically installs for $2.75-$5.50 per square foot versus roughly $6-$10 for 12-18 inch porcelain tile, per local 2026 ranges. LVP is cheaper and faster to replace between tenants; tile lasts longer under heavy traffic but costs more up front and takes longer to redo.

item.title: How Long Does It Take to Replace the Floors in a Whole House?
item.description: A two-person crew lays about 1,000 square feet of click LVP in one to two days on a flat, prepped slab. Tile and glue-down wood take longer because of cure times: tile needs 24 hours before grouting and up to 72 hours before heavy loads, and a full hardwood sand-and-refinish runs three to five working days.

item.title: How Many Days Should You Budget for Refinishing?
item.description: A full hardwood floor sand-and-refinish takes 3-5 working days from the first sanding pass to the last coat. Oil-based polyurethane needs up to 30 days to fully cure before furniture and rugs go back down, and Sarasota's summer humidity can stretch that further, so we build extra dry time into jobs scheduled June through September.

item.title: How Long Does a Slab Need to Dry After Flooding Before New Floors Go In?
item.description: There's no universal number of days, despite what general guides claim. A flooded slab is ready when it tests at or below 75% relative humidity (ASTM F2170) or 3 lbs per 1,000 sq ft per 24 hours (ASTM F1869), the same default limits any new slab-on-grade flooring install needs to meet in a Sarasota-area home, whether or not a flood was ever involved.

item.title: How Long Does Flooring Need to Acclimate in Florida Before Installation?
item.description: There's no set number of days. The NWFA judges acclimation by moisture-meter readings, not a calendar, and only starts counting once the HVAC has run at normal living conditions for at least 48 hours. Strip flooring needs to land within 4% moisture content of the subfloor, wide plank within 2%, before installation in a Sarasota-area home.

item.title: Can I Live in My House During Floor Removal and Installation?
item.description: Yes, most Sarasota-area homeowners stay in the house during a floor replacement. A two-person crew clears about 1,000 square feet of click LVP in one to two days, so we work room by room, sealing off finished areas and containing dust, and most families are back to normal in a zone within a day or two.

item.title: Is Laminate Flooring a Bad Idea in Florida Homes?
item.description: Not automatically, but it needs the right product and prep: Sarasota's outdoor humidity averages 74% year-round, and standard laminate swells if moisture reaches its core. Water-resistant laminate with a WetProtect-style warranty covers spills, pet accidents and wet mopping, but excludes flooding and standing water. Over concrete, Mohawk requires a 6-mil polyethylene moisture barrier with 8-inch overlapped seams before any laminate goes down.

item.title: How Do I Keep Beach Sand From Scratching My Floors?
item.description: Shaw's vinyl care guide recommends cleaning weekly, using mats without latex or rubber backing (which can discolor vinyl), and adding felt protectors under furniture to keep grit from grinding into the finish. A 20-mil wear layer also holds up to sand better than the standard 12-mil grade. For Sarasota-area beach traffic, a weekly vacuum or dry mop before wet-cleaning removes grit before it gets ground in.

item.title: Can New Flooring Go Over Your Existing Tile?
item.description: Yes, in most cases. Rigid-core flooring can go over existing tile if the tile is fully adhered, clean, and flat within 3/16 inch over 10 feet. If it fails that flatness test or has loose or cracked tiles, removal typically runs $2.50-$4.50 per square foot, more on a thick mortar bed, before the new floor goes down.

item.title: Can You Install Hardwood Flooring Directly on a Concrete Slab?
item.description: Engineered hardwood can glue directly to a concrete slab that tests at or below 75% relative humidity (ASTM F2170) or 3 lbs per 1,000 sq ft per 24 hours (ASTM F1869). Solid hardwood traditionally needs a built-up plywood subfloor over the slab first, since the NWFA advises against installing solid wood below grade or directly on bare concrete in a Sarasota-area home.

item.title: What Indoor Humidity Should I Keep for Wood Floors in Florida?
item.description: Keep indoor relative humidity between 30% and 50%, per NWFA guidelines, with temperature around 60-80°F, to protect hardwood and engineered floors in Sarasota and Manatee County homes. Outdoor air here averages about 74% RH year-round, climbing to roughly 78% in August, so a well-sized AC system running consistently does most of the work.
